introduction: A welcome between old friends becomes a crisis when Leontes, King of Sicilia, suspects his wife Hermione and the visiting King of Bohemia of betraying him. His certainty grows without proof, placing his family and loyal servants under impossible demands. The consequences spread far beyond the court, into a pastoral world where another generation confronts royal authority. Moving between accusation, loss and the passage of time, the play asks what can be repaired when trust has been violently broken.

fullSynopsis.text: Leontes, King of Sicilia, suddenly interprets his pregnant wife Hermione's hospitality to his childhood friend Polixenes as adultery. Hermione has persuaded the visiting Bohemian king to stay when Leontes could not. Nothing confirms the suspicion, and Camillo resists it, but Leontes orders him to poison Polixenes. Camillo pretends agreement, then warns the intended victim and escapes with him to Bohemia. Leontes takes their flight as proof of a conspiracy against his marriage and crown, separates Hermione from their son Mamillius and imprisons her despite his courtiers' protests.

Hermione gives birth prematurely to a daughter. Paulina, wife of Antigonus, brings the baby to Leontes, arguing that its likeness proves his paternity and courageously denouncing his jealousy. He orders the child burned, then yields only enough to require Antigonus to abandon her beyond his dominions. At Hermione's public trial, she defends her honour and appeals to Apollo's oracle. Its answer declares her chaste, Polixenes blameless and Camillo faithful, condemns Leontes as a tyrant, and says he will lack an heir unless what is lost is found. Leontes rejects it.

News that Mamillius has died in distress over his mother immediately overturns Leontes's certainty. Hermione collapses, and Paulina later declares her dead. Leontes admits his injustice and vows daily mourning. In coastal Bohemia, Antigonus abandons the infant with identifying materials and gold, naming her Perdita after a dream of Hermione. A bear pursues him, while a storm destroys his ship; a shepherd's son reports both catastrophes. An old shepherd discovers the child, and he and his son take her and the treasure home. Time, appearing as Chorus, then carries the action forward sixteen years.

Perdita grows up as the shepherd's daughter and loves Florizel, Polixenes's son, who visits disguised as Doricles. Camillo longs to return to Sicilia, but Polixenes instead recruits him to investigate the prince's absences. Disguised, they attend the sheep-shearing feast where Perdita presides. The rogue Autolycus, having already picked the shepherd's son's pocket, entertains the company with wares and songs while robbing more purses. Florizel publicly pledges himself to Perdita. When he refuses to consult his father, Polixenes reveals himself, threatens the shepherd and Perdita, and forbids the unequal match.

Florizel remains faithful and determines to flee with Perdita. Camillo directs them to Leontes, coaching them to pretend they come with Polixenes's blessing; secretly he plans to tell Polixenes their destination so he can follow him home. Florizel exchanges clothes with Autolycus to escape unnoticed. Wearing the prince's better garments, Autolycus passes for a courtier and frightens the shepherd and his son into paying for his help. They carry the tokens found with Perdita to prove she is not their kin. Autolycus takes them aboard Florizel's ship, inadvertently bringing the evidence needed to recover her identity.

In Sicilia, Leontes still mourns, and Paulina binds him not to remarry without her consent. He welcomes Florizel and the supposed princess, but news of Polixenes's arrival exposes their flight. Leontes agrees to plead for them. Gentlemen then report the discovery that Perdita is his daughter, established by Hermione's mantle and jewel, Antigonus's letters and the shepherd's account. The kings reconcile and accept the young couple's betrothal. Paulina learns how Antigonus died, while the shepherd and his son gain the standing of gentlemen and promise to assist Autolycus after his pledge to reform.

Paulina takes the reunited company to see what she presents as a statue of Hermione. Leontes wonders at its aged, lifelike appearance. At Paulina's instruction and with music, Hermione moves, embraces him and blesses Perdita. She explains that she preserved herself because the oracle sustained hope of her daughter's survival; the details of her long concealment remain untold. Leontes asks pardon and proposes Camillo as a husband for the widowed Paulina. The company leaves to exchange its missing histories, recovering family and friendship without reversing the deaths of Mamillius and Antigonus.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: Camillo and Archidamus celebrate the longstanding friendship of Leontes and Polixenes and the promise of Leontes's son Mamillius. After nine months in Sicilia, Polixenes insists he must return to Bohemia. Leontes asks Hermione to persuade him to stay; when she succeeds, he abruptly reads their friendly intimacy as evidence that she has betrayed him. He examines Mamillius's likeness to himself and pressures Camillo to agree with his suspicions. Camillo insists that Hermione is honourable, but Leontes demands that he poison the visiting king. Outwardly consenting, Camillo instead resolves to leave court rather than commit murder. He warns Polixenes, explains the danger of trying to reason with Leontes's settled jealousy, and arranges a secret departure with the king and his followers. Polixenes trusts the warning and promises Camillo protection in his service.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: Leontes interrupts Hermione and Mamillius after hearing that Polixenes and Camillo have fled, treating their escape as proof of treason. He removes the boy, accuses Hermione of carrying Polixenes's child and sends her to prison. His lords defend her without success; he says messengers have been sent to Apollo's oracle to confirm the matter. At the prison, Paulina learns that Hermione has given birth early to a healthy daughter. She undertakes to carry the infant to the King, hoping its innocence will soften him. Leontes remains consumed by revenge while Mamillius grows ill. Paulina brings the child, defends its likeness to him and challenges his conduct. Leontes threatens her, then orders Antigonus to burn the baby. The lords' entreaties change the sentence to abandonment in a remote place beyond Sicilia. News of the oracle's messengers prompts preparations for Hermione's trial.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Cleomenes and Dion return from Delphos, hoping the oracle will vindicate Hermione. At trial she rejects both adultery and conspiracy, explaining that she welcomed Polixenes in obedience to her husband and valued Camillo as an honest man. Apollo's answer declares her innocent, affirms the baby's legitimacy and condemns Leontes; it also denies him an heir unless the lost is found. He calls the oracle false, but the immediate report of Mamillius's death makes him acknowledge divine judgment. Hermione faints, and Paulina later announces her death. Leontes confesses his intended murder of Polixenes and vows perpetual mourning. In Bohemia, Antigonus leaves the baby, gold and identifying tokens, naming her Perdita according to a dream he recounts. A bear pursues him offstage; the shepherd's son reports his death and the shipwreck. An old shepherd finds the child, and the two take her and the treasure home.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Time asks the audience to pass over sixteen years, leaving Leontes in grief and introducing Perdita's life as a shepherd's daughter. Camillo wishes to return to Sicilia, but Polixenes draws him into a disguised visit to discover why Florizel frequents the shepherd's home. Autolycus feigns injury to steal the shepherd's son's purse, then sells ballads and trinkets at the sheep-shearing feast while picking pockets. Perdita hosts the celebration, and Florizel, calling himself Doricles, declares his love. Their intended contract collapses when the disguised Polixenes demands paternal consultation, reveals himself and threatens the apparently lowborn bride. Camillo helps the steadfast lovers flee toward Sicilia with a fabricated diplomatic story, while planning to guide Polixenes after them. Autolycus exchanges clothes with Florizel, impersonates a courtier, and takes payment from the terrified shepherd and son to bring them aboard with Perdita's identifying tokens.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: Leontes resists his courtiers' wish that he remarry and swears to let Paulina choose any future wife. Florizel arrives with Perdita, pretending to bring his father's greetings and presenting her as a princess. News that Polixenes has followed exposes their flight; Leontes nevertheless offers to advocate for their love. Gentlemen report that the shepherd's evidence has established Perdita as Leontes's lost daughter, fulfilling the oracle and reconciling the kings. Paulina's joy is mixed with confirmation of Antigonus's death. The shepherd and his son enjoy their new gentility, while Autolycus seeks their support. At Paulina's house the company views Hermione standing as a statue. Paulina calls for faith and music; Hermione descends alive, embraces Leontes and blesses Perdita. She says hope for her daughter preserved her. Leontes proposes Camillo for Paulina and asks her to lead the reunited families away to exchange their histories.
